headline: Sensex ends above 81,900 amid FII inflows; October retail inflation breaches RBI's 6% upper limit

marketStatus.message: Market is open for trading today.

why: Foreign Institutional Investor (FII) inflows provided significant support to the Indian markets
Lower crude oil prices helped boost investor sentiment during the trading session
Banking stocks led a rebound in early trade, helping the indices recover
Retail inflation in October surged to 6.09%, breaching the RBI's upper tolerance band for the first time in two years
whatHappening: The Sensex closed above the 81,900 mark, extending its winning streak to a third consecutive day
The Indian Rupee fell 33 paise to hit a record low of 94.04 against the U.S. dollar
Nifty 50 ended the session near 25,229, while the Nifty Smallcap 100 outperformed the broader market
Ola Electric reported a narrowed Q2 loss of Rs 362 crore, though revenue saw a decline
summary: Indian benchmarks extended gains for a third session with the Sensex closing above 81,900, supported by foreign fund inflows and lower oil prices. However, economic data showed retail inflation hitting a two-year high of 6.09%, while the Rupee weakened to 94.04 against the dollar. Corporate earnings remained in focus as Ola Electric narrowed its losses and Oil India reported a 36% drop in profit.
